summary: This ECMWF Confluence page (from the EMOSLIB documentation) explains Gaussian and reduced Gaussian grids. A Gaussian grid is a latitude/longitude grid with irregular but Equator-symmetric latitude spacing, and it is referred to by its number N, the count of latitude lines between a Pole and the Equator. In a regular grid each latitude has 4*N longitude points, while a reduced grid specifies a variable number per latitude, with ECMWF choosing counts of the form 2^p * 3^q * 5^r so the east-west grid length stays roughly constant. The page also notes that custom grids can be supplied via the 'g_lats' and 'g_pts' options, and it lists common N values from N32 to N640. The page notes that EMOSLIB is now deprecated.
one_line: Explains Gaussian and reduced Gaussian latitude/longitude grids used by ECMWF, including point-count rules and custom grid options in EMOSLIB.
key_facts: A Gaussian grid is a latitude/longitude grid whose latitude spacing is irregular but symmetrical about the Equator.
A Gaussian grid has no latitude line at either Pole or at the Equator.
A Gaussian grid is usually referred to by its number N, which is the number of lines of latitude between a Pole and the Equator.
In a regular Gaussian grid, the number of longitude points along a latitude is 4*N.
In a reduced Gaussian grid, the number of longitude points along each latitude is specified and may differ between latitudes.
A reduced Gaussian grid may also be called a quasi-regular Gaussian grid.
In ECMWF reduced grids, the number of points on each latitude row is chosen so the local east-west grid length remains approximately constant for all latitudes.
ECMWF point counts must be suitable for the Fast Fourier Transform, meaning number = 2^p * 3^q * 5^r.
The FFT is used to interpolate spectral fields to grid point fields.
The gaussian latitude values can be supplied as an array using the option 'g_lats'.
The number of points along each latitude line can be supplied as an array using the option 'g_pts'.
A custom grid definition is allowed as long as the resulting grid definition is self-consistent.
The page lists standard Gaussian grid numbers including N32, N48, N80, N128, N160, N200, N256, N320, N400, N512 and N640.
The page was created by Unknown User (mas) and last modified by Umberto Modigliani on Jan 20, 2013.
The EMOSLIB space is marked as deprecated ("Emoslib is now deprecated").
